questions.question: The energy price cap limits…
options: The unit rates and standing charges on default tariffs
questions.explanation: It caps rates, not your total bill. Use more and you pay more.

questions.question: An energy standing charge is…
options: A fixed daily charge, however much you use
questions.explanation: You pay it even if you use no energy.

questions.question: Who sets the energy price cap?
questions.explanation: Ofgem reviews the cap regularly.

questions.question: When a broadband or mobile contract ends, prices often…
options: Rise unless you renegotiate or switch
questions.explanation: Providers must tell you when your contract ends, so use that to haggle.

questions.question: A SIM-only deal makes the most sense when…
options: You own your phone and don't need a new one
You want a free new phone
questions.explanation: Keeping your phone and going SIM-only is often far cheaper.

questions.question: The council tax discount for a single adult living alone is…
questions.explanation: Adults living alone usually get 25% off.

questions.question: Option 1: a phone contract at £45/month for 24 months. Option 2: buy the phone for £600 plus SIM-only at £12/month. How much does option 2 save over 24 months?
Broadband “social tariffs” are for…
options: People on certain benefits, such as Universal Credit
questions.explanation: They're cheaper packages for eligible households.

questions.question: A water meter often saves money when…
options: Fewer people live in the home than there are bedrooms
questions.explanation: Smaller households often pay less on a meter.

questions.question: Paying for energy by monthly Direct Debit is usually…
options: Cheaper than paying when the bill arrives
questions.explanation: Suppliers usually charge less for Direct Debit.

questions.question: When you switch energy supplier, your supply…
options: Isn't interrupted: it uses the same pipes and wires
Is cut off for a day
questions.explanation: Only the company billing you changes.

questions.question: A fixed-rate energy tariff means…
options: Your unit rates are fixed for a period
Your total bill is fixed, however much you use
questions.explanation: Use more and you still pay more, but at a fixed rate per unit.

questions.question: Leaving devices on standby…
questions.explanation: Switching off at the wall stops standby use.

questions.question: Getting car insurance quotes about 3–4 weeks before renewal is often…
options: Cheaper than buying on the last day
questions.explanation: Comparison data suggests last-minute quotes are often pricier.

questions.question: Since 2022, UK home and car insurers must…
options: Not charge renewing customers more than new customers for the same policy
questions.explanation: The FCA banned “price walking”, though shopping around can still save money.

questions.question: Your water meter shows a sudden big jump, but your usage hasn't changed. It could be…
questions.explanation: Ask your water company about leak checks and allowances.

questions.question: Since 17 January 2025, price rises in new broadband and mobile contracts must be…
options: Shown in pounds and pence upfront
questions.explanation: Price rises in new contracts must be shown in pounds and pence upfront.

questions.question: A £600 phone plus £12 a month SIM-only for 24 months costs how much in total?
questions.explanation: £600 + (12 x £24) = £888, versus a £45 a month contract at £1,080.

questions.question: You live alone as the only adult. What is the usual council tax discount?
questions.explanation: Living alone usually gets 25% off council tax.

questions.question: You think your council tax band is too high. Who can you check with in England and Wales?
questions.explanation: You can check with the Valuation Office Agency, but bands can go up as well as down.

questions.question: Since January 2022, can insurers charge renewing customers more than new customers for the same policy?
options: No, for home and car insurance
questions.explanation: Home and car insurers can't charge renewing customers more than a new customer for the same policy.

questions.question: Why is paying insurance monthly often dearer?
questions.explanation: Monthly payments often include interest, so pay annually if you can.
